description: FIND usages of a name written on a line no recorder tokenised. Every posting-fed tier — exact, substring, and the split-parts map — can only answer where some recorder produced a token, and the body of an .rst literal block produces none. A name written inside one therefore answered zero however plainly the file contained it, which reads exactly like 'this name is not used here'. The files themselves are now read for every query, so the line's own text decides. These cases pin the site that was invisible, the token boundary that keeps reading files from turning a precise query into a substring search, and a control that must stay empty. The boundary is Unicode-aware — a letter, digit or underscore in any script continues a token — so that a find and the MATCHING WORD sweep it arms agree about where a token starts and ends; the ASCII-only form of that test reported sites the sweep would then refuse to rewrite, and is pinned against in the unit tests beside `holds`.

cases.name: a_name_on_a_line_no_recorder_tokenised_is_found
cases.why: line 228 of doc/services/pm/device.rst is '#define DT_DRV_COMPAT dummy_device', inside a '.. code-block:: c' literal block. Nothing posts a token for that block's own text — 'gpio_callback' three lines below IS posted, because the grammar gives it a nested node of its own — so no posting-fed tier could reach line 228. Verified answering zero on the deployed engine before this change.

cases.name: an_identifier_still_answers_as_a_token_not_as_a_substring
cases.why: the discriminating case for reading files at all: 'DT_DRV' occurs in that file only inside 'DT_DRV_COMPAT' on line 228. A scan that matched substrings would report it and quietly redefine what FIND usages means; the boundary is the one MATCHING WORD uses, so a sweep rewrites exactly the sites the find listed.

cases.name: a_name_absent_from_the_corpus_still_answers_zero
cases.why: reading every file must not invent sites: completeness is only worth something if empty still means empty.

cases.name: a_name_living_only_in_a_file_the_index_tracks_by_path_is_found
cases.why: the workspace holds three kinds of file — ones that produced symbols, ones tracked by path and size alone, and ones added this session — and the read pass originally walked only the first and the third. A .gitignore is the second kind, so line 23 of the root one ('cscope.*') was reachable by nothing: 'FIND usages OF cscope' answered zero corpus-wide on the deployed engine, which is what an agent reads as safe to rename. The scope is the root file alone, so the pin does not move when another .gitignore elsewhere mentions the same pattern.

cases.name: a_configuration_file_that_sets_a_flag_is_a_usage_site
cases.why: the case that makes this matter rather than merely tidy. A prj.conf line reading CONFIG_PM_DEVICE_RUNTIME=y is the canonical place a Kconfig option is turned on, and .conf is an extension no plugin claims — so every project configuration enabling a flag was absent from that flag's blast radius, and a rename would have left them all behind. Line 4 of the same file is CONFIG_PM_DEVICE_RUNTIME_DEFAULT_ENABLE=y, which must NOT match: the token boundary has to hold in the newly reachable files too, or reading them would have traded one wrong answer for another.
